name: 100 Years (1926|2026) XXL crane
description: Fuselage: Lufthansa dark blue, with a huge white stylized crane over it: its beak just behind the flight deck, its neck running aft along the upper fuselage under a blue crown (on the 747 the hump stays blue above it), a slim blue sliver inside the neck pointing forward, its body filling the side and crown over and behind the wing root so the airliner's wings read as the crane's, and its legs trailing low aft under a big blue wedge whose point sits near the wing's trailing edge at the window line and whose edges sweep up to the crown ahead of the fin and down to the belly. The belly is blue from the nose to just behind the wing, ending rounded, with a white '100' on it; white behind it. Tail: standard Lufthansa dark-blue fin with the white crane in a white ring. Engines: white cowlings. Winglets: white. Titles: white 'Lufthansa' under the windows behind door 1, a small white crane-in-ring under the cockpit; huge grey '100' (with a faint grey crane drawing above its '1') on the left over the blue wedge's point, and grey '1926 | 2026' along the windows on the right, the divider at the wedge's point. Colors hex: Lufthansa Blue is published in the 2018 brand as #05164D (paint match unverified); the numerals' grey measured off press photos in evening light, approximate.

notes: Same design on D-ABYN (B748), D-ABPU (B789), D-AIXL (A359), D-AING (A20N) and the A380 D-AIMH; an A350-1000 due autumn 2026, and the newsroom (4 March 2026) counts a second A320neo. Drawn 2026-11-22: the scheme's own geometry is the 747-8I's (D-ABYN), measured on Commons photos fitted to shapes/B748-passenger.json and on three Lufthansa newsroom press photos (measured only); `drawnOn` names B748 (the schema takes designators; the 747-8I's own shape gets the same paint exactly through `types.B748-passenger`). The A350-900, 787-9 and A320neo carry the design adapted to each type (where the neck starts, the crown's blue, the wedge's point), each measured on its own airframe's photos in `types`. The A380 D-AIMH isn't measured: it draws the 747's geometry fitted by landmarks, which won't place the crane between its decks as painted. Not drawn: the faint grey crane drawing above the '100' on the left, the small crane beside the belly '100' on the A320neo, the registration, flags and door marks. On the 747 the hump's blue top over the neck's front is approximate: an upper deck wears the crown's paint carried up, so the white beak can't reach onto the hump as it does on the aircraft.

A359.note: D-AIXL (A350-900), measured on its own photos fitted to shapes/A359.json: the neck starts square behind the flight deck (not pointed as on the 747) with a step in its top edge; the crown stays blue to the wing; the aft wedge's point is under the wing's trailing edge, its top edge reaching the crown well ahead of the fin. Where the wing hides the side (the crown blue's end, the sliver's aft end, the white's lower edge at the wing root) the 747's shapes were followed.
